jobs.description:
Company Description

Algen is an AI-native precision medicine company harnessing the power of CRISPR and functional genomics to transform drug discovery and development. A spin-out from the laboratory of Nobel Laureate Professor Jennifer Doudna, Algen was founded at the forefront of gene-editing innovation. We combine cutting-edge CRISPR technologies with advanced AI approaches to systematically modulate disease biology at scale and accelerate the path to effective treatments. Join us in redefining what's possible in AI-powered drug discovery.

Job Description

As an Agentic AI Engineer (Life Science), you’ll build the software that lets an AI agent plan a scientific analysis, choose tools and recover when a step fails. You’ll work with biologists and chemists to define what a successful analysis looks like, then use those criteria to decide which changes to ship. The work includes bringing the latest advances and original ideas into production. The ideal candidate combines strong engineering execution with a quantitative mindset and an interest in AI agents for scientific discovery.

Responsibilities

Advance the agent harness by bringing the latest research and open-source developments into production and experimenting with new approaches to multi-agent coordination, model routing, memory, planning, and tool use.
Work with biologists and chemists to turn real research questions into test cases. Agree on what evidence an answer needs and record the steps a scientist would need to check it.
Compare changes against a baseline on representative tasks. Measure scientific correctness, completion rate, latency and cost before deciding whether to release a change.
Make long-running analyses resilient. Run code in a sandbox with scoped tool access, save progress and let interrupted jobs resume without repeating completed work.
Trace production failures from the agent’s decision through its tool calls and outputs. Reproduce the failure, fix it and add a test that catches it on the next release.

Qualifications

MUST HAVE:
2+ years of industry experience building production software, with hands-on ownership of a backend service, infrastructure component or full-stack feature.
MUST HAVE:
Familiarity with LLM APIs, tool calling, agent runtimes, or workflow orchestration.
MUST HAVE:
Research or production experience building an LLM-powered agent that calls tools or coordinates a workflow. You can explain a design choice you made and how you tested it.
MUST HAVE:
Experience using data to judge a system change. You can design a repeatable comparison, investigate inconsistent results and explain the tradeoffs to colleagues.
Ability to take an engineering problem from design through testing, deployment and debugging, and to write code that teammates can maintain.
Ability to move between research questions, data analysis, system design, and production implementation.
Experience or strong interest in AI for science, scientific agents, computational research, or automated scientific discovery.
Experience building modern web applications (e.g. React, TypeScript, FastAPI, or similar frameworks).
Ability to move fast, own features end-to-end, and operate with high autonomy.
High standards for code quality, maintainability, and engineering excellence. .

Preferred

Experience designing benchmarks for LLMs, reviewing outputs with domain experts or replaying past runs to test for regressions.
Experience with durable workflows, task queues, sandboxed code execution or tools for inspecting distributed jobs.
Experience with LLM post-training, including fine-tuning models for tool use or scientific tasks
Experience developing agent systems for scientific discovery, particularly self-evolving agents.
Research or graduate-level experience in machine learning, computational biology or another quantitative field.

jobs.description:
We’re ALTEN Technology USA, an engineering company helping clients bring groundbreaking ideas to life—from advancing space exploration and life-saving medical devices to building autonomous electric vehicles. Workplace:
On-site, 5 days per week
Location:
San Francisco, CA (Dogpatch neighborhood) 
Salary:
$90,000-$105,000
We are seeking a Robotics Lab Technician to be the versatile builder at the center of our prototype lab. You'll move fluidly between precision assembly, wiring and electrical integration, system bring-up, and acceptance testing to take robots from a kit of parts to a validated, working system. You'll install software and read logs, bridging the gap between hardware and software during bring-up, and you’ll troubleshoot and solve integration issues during testing and validation. We're looking for someone careful with their hands, organized about documentation, and comfortable collaborating with mechanical, electrical, controls, and software engineers in a fast-iterating environment.
Key Job Responsibilities

    • Assemble electromechanical robotic systems and subsystems (actuators, gearboxes, sensors, vision systems, wiring harnesses, PCBAs) from mechanical drawings, schematics, and work instructions, following torque specs and assembly procedures.
    • Kit parts against the BOM, stage hardware and fixtures, and set up assembly jigs and alignment rigs for each build.
    • Build first articles from prototype kits, provide engineering with actionable build feedback (DFx), and execute rework and engineering change orders (ECOs) as designs iterate.
    • Fabricate, route, and terminate wiring harnesses to documented pinouts with proper strain relief, bend radius management, and cable routing for moving assemblies.
    • Perform pre-power-on electrical verification (continuity, pinout, insulation, polarity) and board-level integration under ESD discipline.
    • Maintain build records, travelers, inspection checklists, and non-conformance reports (NCRs) ensuring full traceability. Redline and improve work instructions with each build.
    • Bring up newly built assemblies, verify actuator and sensor function, and run acceptance testing and performance characterization using standard and custom test equipment.
    • Use git and the Linux command line to install, configure, and run test and calibration software on robots; track software versions across the fleet.
    • Read logs and source code well enough to localize problems and provide engineering with actionable triage reports.
    • Collaborate with engineering to isolate integration issues, narrow root cause across mechanical, electrical, and software domains, and drive corrective actions into work instructions.
    • Keep the lab safe, organized, and ESD-compliant; track tooling, consumables, and inventory.
    • Drive continuous improvement and support prototype-to-production transitions by developing SOPs, assembly aids, and training materials.

Required Qualifications

    • 3-5+ years of hands-on experience assembling and testing electromechanical systems such as robotics hardware, precision mechatronic assemblies, aerospace/automotive hardware, or electronics assembly in a lab, prototype, or manufacturing environment.
    • Able to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and written work instructions to build and test complex hardware.
    • Proficient with hand and torque tools, basic crimping and soldering, and steady work with small fasteners and connectors.
    • Demonstrated ability to perform functional and acceptance testing using standard test equipment such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, and power supplies.
    • Experience performing quality inspections and maintaining detailed build records, including assembly travelers, inspection checklists, and non-conformance documentation.
    • Comfortable at a Linux command line running scripts, and willing to grow those skills.
    • Knowledge of ESD handling procedures and lab safety protocols for working with high-voltage electronics and heavy mechanical assemblies.
    • Clear communication, careful record-keeping, and safe work habits.

Preferred Qualifications

    • Associate's degree or technical certification in Electronics Technology, Mechatronics, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent hands-on experience.
    • Experience assembling and testing robotic systems with high degrees of freedom, including familiarity with actuators, force/torque sensors, IMUs, encoders, and vision/camera systems.
    • Wiring harness fabrication experience including building to a pinout, connector assembly, and cable routing on moving assemblies.
    • Background in a robotics research lab, hardware startup, aerospace, or advanced electromechanical environment where rapid prototyping and tight engineering collaboration are standard.
    • Mechatronics training/coursework or electromechanical troubleshooting experience.
    • Some scripting ability (Python or bash) for test and calibration; basic familiarity with git, Docker, or networking.
    • Experience with ERP systems, MES, PLM, or lab management tools for tracking inventory, build status, component traceability, and hardware/software revision control.
Work Environment & Physical Requirements

    • On-site lab role; standing, bench work, and hands-on assembly for extended periods, including work in awkward positions and tight spaces.
    • Fine motor precision and close-vision work with small fasteners, connectors, and board-level components.
    • Lifting and maneuvering heavy robotic assemblies; use of required PPE.
    • Work around high-voltage electronics, powered actuators, and moving machinery.

Salary Range

Strong interpersonal skills
